heading: Auditing iOS Keychain and Biometric Bypasses in Production
core_technical_idea: Demonstrate the structural security divergence between vulnerable local biometric UI gates and Secure Enclave hardware-bound cryptographic keys.
must_show: LocalAuthentication LAContext UI gate separate from Keychain storage
Secure Enclave hardware-bound keys with kSecAccessControlBiometryAny
composition: Side-by-side comparative architecture flow showing an insecure UI-only biometric check versus a secure hardware-backed cryptographic enclave check.
alt_text: Architectural diagram comparing insecure local biometric UI gates against hardware-bound Secure Enclave cryptographic protection in iOS Keychain.
caption: Biometric prompts act merely as local UI gates unless explicitly bound to Secure Enclave cryptographic keys via SecAccessControl.
mermaid_code:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Insecure [Vulnerable UI Gate Pattern]
        A[FaceID / TouchID Prompt] -->|LAContext Success| B[Local App State Unlocked]
        B -->|Tokens Stored With| C[kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock]
        C -->|Readable in Memory| D[Persistent Session Exposure]
    end

    subgraph Secure [Hardware-Bound Cryptographic Pattern]
        E[FaceID / TouchID Prompt] -->|SecAccessControl| F[Secure Enclave]
        F -->|Requires BiometryAny / CurrentSet| G[Cryptographic Key Decryption]
        G -->|Success| H[Secure Token Access]
    end

    style Insecure fill:#ffebee,stroke:#c62828,stroke-width:2px
    style Secure fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px

heading: Mapping Keychain Accessibility Classes to Data Protection Risk
core_technical_idea: Visualizing the inverse relationship between Keychain accessibility attributes and their associated data protection risk scores, highlighting memory persistence windows.
must_show: Keychain accessibility attributes mapped to risk values
Clear distinction between hardware-backed vs after-first-unlock persistence
composition: Horizontal bar chart ordered by risk score descending, with color coding indicating high vulnerability (red) to maximum security (green).
alt_text: Horizontal bar chart comparing iOS Keychain accessibility attributes against their data protection risk scores from 1 to 10.
caption: Risk escalation profile across iOS Keychain accessibility classes, showing how persistence after device lock drastically elevates attack surface risk.

chart_spec.title: Keychain Accessibility Attributes vs. Data Protection Risk Score

heading: Decoupling LocalAuthentication Success from Persistent Storage
core_technical_idea: Demonstrating how a decoupled LAContext boolean gate allows direct Keychain queries without cryptographic binding, bypassing secure access control.
composition: Top-to-bottom sequence and data flow showing the decoupled pathways between the LocalAuthentication check and the independent Keychain query.
alt_text: Sequence diagram illustrating the vulnerable iOS anti-pattern where LAContext acts as a boolean gate independent of SecItemCopyMatching.
caption: The architectural anti-pattern: treating LocalAuthentication as a boolean gate rather than tying access control directly to the Keychain item.
mermaid_code:
flowchart TD
    A[User Action] --> B[LAContext evaluatePolicy]
    B -->|Returns Success (true)| C[SecItemCopyMatching]
    C --> D[(Keychain Storage
No SecAccessControl)]
    style B fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:#ff9999,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

heading: Building Frida Runtime Instrumentation Workflows for Interception
core_technical_idea: The execution flow and data extraction pathway when Frida hooks SecItemCopyMatching to audit iOS Keychain queries.
must_show: Frida Interceptor attaching to Security framework
ObjC Object parameter extraction and JSON messaging back to host
composition: Top-down sequence flow showing the interaction between the Python runner, the Frida runtime hook inside the target process, and the intercepted Keychain query data.
alt_text: Diagram showing the Frida instrumentation workflow: Python generates the hook, Frida attaches to SecItemCopyMatching, intercepts query parameters via Objective-C runtime, and transmits event details back to the host.
caption: Runtime instrumentation pipeline demonstrating how Frida intercepts `SecItemCopyMatching` calls to extract and inspect Keychain query attributes.
mermaid_code:
flowchart TD
    A[Python Runner Script] -->|Generates Hook| B(Frida Runtime)
    B -->|Module.findExportByName| C{Security Framework}
    C -->|SecItemCopyMatching found| D[Interceptor.attach]
    D -->|onEnter: Extract args[0]| E[ObjC.Object Parameter Mapping]
    E -->|send() payload| F[process_runtime_event]
    F -->|Print Audit Log| G[Terminal Output]

heading: Extracting Sensitive Tokens Before Biometric Evaluation Executes
core_technical_idea: Demonstrating how low-level C APIs bypass high-level LAContext biometric UI prompts by querying the Keychain database directly.
must_show: LAContext UI Prompt (Face ID / Touch ID)
composition: Two parallel execution paths showing the secure intended path gated by LAContext versus the direct bypass path via SecItemCopyMatching to the Keychain database.
alt_text: Mermaid sequence diagram comparing the secure UI-gated authentication flow with the direct Keychain background extraction vulnerability.
caption: Low-level C APIs can query the Keychain directly, completely bypassing the LAContext biometric evaluation layer.
mermaid_code:
flowchart TD
    subgraph App["Application Process"]
        direction TB
        Logic["Swift / Objective-C App Logic"]
        LAC["LAContext Biometric Prompt"]
        LowAPI["Low-Level C API (SecItemCopyMatching)"]
    end

    subgraph Storage["Keychain Database"]
        KC["Encrypted Payload Storage"]
    end

    Logic -->|"Invokes"| LAC
    LAC -->|"Success Callback Required"| Logic
    
    LowAPI -->|"Direct Query (Bypasses UI)"| KC
    KC -->|"Returns Payload if kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock"| LowAPI

    style LAC fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style LowAPI fill:#ff9999,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style KC fill:#99ccff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

heading: Hardening Production Codebases Against Automated Runtime Attacks
core_technical_idea: Hardware-level cryptographic binding between the Secure Enclave, biometric validation flags, and keychain items to prevent runtime bypasses.
composition: Top-down sequence flow showing application request crossing the hardware boundary into the Secure Enclave with biometric enforcement.
alt_text: Mermaid sequence diagram illustrating how SecAccessControl binds keychain items to the Secure Enclave and enforces biometric validation at the hardware level.
caption: Hardware-enforced isolation: biometric prompts and key decryption occur entirely within the Secure Enclave, isolating them from application-level execution flow.
mermaid_code:
flowchart TD
    A[Application Code] -->|SecItemAdd / SecItemCopyMatching| B(SecAccessControl
.biometryCurrentSet)
    subgraph Secure Enclave [Hardware Boundary]
        B --> C{Biometric Profile Valid?}
        C -->|Match| D[Release Decryption Key]
        C -->|Enrollment Changed| E[Invalidate Key / Return Error]
    end
    D --> F[Secure Token Access]
    E --> G[Access Denied]
